meta.name: Send Russian joke comics to Telegram with OpenRouter and Google Sheets

parameters.content:
## Anekdot -> Image -> Telegram
Pipeline: Google Sheets (page/dedup state) -> anekdot.ru scraping -> AI Agent (Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, JSON with characters) -> Code (prompt assembly) -> OpenRouter Images (Nano Banana 2 Lite) -> Telegram -> log to Used Jokes.

Required credentials: OpenRouter API, Telegram API, Google Sheets OAuth2 (with Sheets API + Drive API enabled).

To run on a schedule, replace Manual Trigger with a Schedule Trigger and activate the workflow.

### ⚠️ SETUP CHECKLIST — configure before first run
1. **Table name** — "Search files and folders" & "Create spreadsheet" (currently "Anekdot Bot — History"). Pick any name; both nodes must match exactly.
2. **Telegram chat ID** — "Send a photo message" (currently placeholder "YOUR_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID"). Replace with your channel/chat numeric ID.
3. **Images folder name** — "Create Images Folder" (currently "Anekdot Bot — Cartoons"). Optional to rename.
4. **Source tag/category** — "Build Page URL" (currently scrapes the "вовочка" tag on anekdot.ru). Change to scrape a different category.
5. **Chat model** — "OpenRouter Chat Model" node has no model preset; select one manually (e.g. google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite).
6. **Image model** — "Generate Image (OpenRouter)" (currently google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image). See the model comparison note near that node before switching.

options.systemMessage:
You extract structured data from a Russian joke (anekdot) for generating a comic-style illustration. Do NOT write a ready-made image prompt — only extract facts as JSON.

Return STRICTLY valid JSON (no markdown, no ```, no explanation before or after) in this format:

{
  "scene": "brief description of the setting and what's happening, in English, 1 sentence",
  "characters": [
    {
      "id": "unique_id_in_latin_letters",
      "descriptionEn": "character's appearance and pose in English, without mentioning their position in the frame",
      "dialogueRu": "short line in Russian (3-5 words) or null",
      "dialogueSafe": true or false,
      "dialogueMasked": "the same line with forbidden words masked, or null",
      "dialogueClean": "a safe paraphrase of dialogueRu in Russian (3-5 words) or null"
    }
  ]
}

Extraction rules:
1. List ALL characters physically present in the scene of the joke — even ones who don't speak. Don't skip anyone.
2. Order of characters in the `characters` array — left to right, as they should stand in the frame.
3. Fill `dialogueRu` only for the FIRST TWO lines of dialogue in the joke, in text order (the first line of direct speech, and — if immediately followed by another character's line — that one too). For all other characters, `dialogueRu` = null.
4. Every line in `dialogueRu`, `dialogueMasked`, and `dialogueClean` must be STRICTLY one short phrase, 3-5 words, never more. This is a hard limit, not a suggestion.
   - If the character's original line in the joke is longer, don't copy it verbatim — compress it to the core idea.
   - Remove repeated forms of address and filler words (e.g. "Marya Ivanovna, Marya Ivanovna, I know how..." → "Marya Ivanovna, I know walruses!").
   - Remove introductory phrases that carry no meaning (interjections like "well", "so", if the line doesn't lose meaning without them).
   - Text — Russian only, do not translate.
   - Don't shorten TO THE POINT of losing the joke's meaning — if 3-5 words genuinely isn't enough to preserve the punchline, use the upper bound or slightly more, but never give a full verbatim, multi-word sentence.
5. If the joke involves physical contact between characters — slaps, hits, fights, etc. — do NOT describe this literally in the `scene` field (avoid words like "hits", "slaps", "spanks", "beats" and similar). Describe a safe comedic equivalent without physical contact — for example, a character makes an exaggerated theatrical gesture or winds up for a swing, but doesn't actually touch the other character.
6. Describe characters' poses and gestures in `scene` and `descriptionEn` ONLY as neutral or comically exaggerated — avoid wording that could read as threatening or tense: "tense", "threatening", "defiant expression", "holding [object] near [body part]", "raising hand to strike", and similar. Even if the joke's plot is conflict-driven, describe it as clearly comedic (exaggerated annoyance, comic indignation), not as a psychologically tense or threatening scene.

`dialogueSafe` rule (VERY IMPORTANT, apply strictly):

For EVERY character with a non-empty `dialogueRu`, assess whether that specific phrase would pass the content-safety moderation of image-generation systems (Google Gemini and similar). Set `dialogueSafe: false` if the phrase contains ANY of the following:
- profanity in any form, including veiled language and euphemisms;
- sexual subtext: direct or implied references to sex, sexual acts, intimate body parts, lewd double meanings — even in casual slang;
- descriptions of violence, threats, physical harm;
- any other content an adult moderator would consider inappropriate for a family audience.

If there's even the slightest doubt — set `dialogueSafe: false`, that's the correct default. Set `dialogueSafe: true` only for unambiguously neutral, decent phrases ("Why?", "That's right, dad", "Well, well" and similar).

`dialogueMasked` rule (REQUIRED if `dialogueSafe: false`):

Take `dialogueRu` and mask ONLY the specific problematic words (profanity, vulgar terms, insults) — keep the rest of the phrase verbatim as in the original.

Masking rules:
- Keep ONLY the first letter of the problematic word; replace all other letters (including the last one) with the "*" symbol, one asterisk per hidden letter.
- If the word is shorter than 3 letters, mask it entirely with the same number of "*".
- Do NOT touch the rest of the phrase — mask only the actual profane/inappropriate words, not the whole line.
- Preserve punctuation, letter case, and sentence structure — the result should visually read like an ordinary "censored" line from a comic.

`dialogueMasked` must always be filled in whenever `dialogueSafe: false` and `dialogueRu` isn't empty. Never leave it null in that case.

`dialogueClean` rule (REQUIRED if `dialogueSafe: false`):

This is the fallback, maximally safe option — a short (3-5 words) neutral phrase in the same grammatical form (question/statement/address to the same recipient) that preserves the COMEDIC SITUATION (who's addressing whom, in what tone, what's happening in the plot), but completely removes profanity, vulgarity, sexual subtext, or violence — not softened with a euphemism, but with the problematic part replaced entirely by a neutral wording.

Examples:
- A question about how to spell a curse word → dialogueClean: "So how is that word spelled?"
- A line insulting a character → dialogueClean: a short phrase with the same tone of indignation, but without the insult, e.g. "How dare you say that!"
- A line threatening physical harm → dialogueClean: a phrase with the same stern tone, but without specifying violence, e.g. "You'll get what's coming to you!"

`dialogueClean` should sound like a natural line the character would say in this scene, not like a censored edit — avoid ellipses "...", the word "censored", or similarly obvious signs of a cut.

`dialogueMasked` and `dialogueClean` are filled in SIMULTANEOUSLY and INDEPENDENTLY of each other whenever `dialogueSafe: false` — the choice between them happens later, not at your level.

Important: Vovochka jokes often rely on crudeness or vulgarity as the punchline itself — that's a normal part of the joke text, and you should not distort the joke's meaning in the `dialogueRu` field. But that specific line must not end up on the image as raw, unprocessed text — that's exactly why `dialogueSafe: false`, `dialogueMasked`, and `dialogueClean` exist.

Write the final scene description (`scene`, `descriptionEn`) in English (the image-generation model interprets composition more accurately in English). But the text inside `dialogueRu`, `dialogueMasked`, and `dialogueClean` — keep strictly in Russian, do not translate it or change it to English.

parameters.content:
## Table Discovery
WHAT: Searches Google Drive for a file named "Anekdot Bot — History".
KEY FIELDS: queryString = "888" (actual table name), output `id` used
by the True branch downstream.
WHY: Lets the workflow run with zero manual setup — no need to
pre-create the spreadsheet before the first run.

## Load State (existing table)
WHAT: Renames the found file's `id` to `documentId` (unified field
name used everywhere downstream), then reads the `State` sheet by
name (not by internal gid — see note below).
KEY FIELDS: documentId, sheet mode = "By Name" = "State".
WHY: "By Name" avoids having to compute the tab's internal gid via
extra API calls — far simpler and equally reliable.

## Extract Scene, Characters & Dialogue
WHAT: Sends the joke text to Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, returns strict
JSON: scene, characters[] with descriptionEn, dialogueRu (3–5 words),
dialogueSafe, dialogueMasked, dialogueClean.
KEY FIELDS: dialogueSafe (model's own moderation self-check),
dialogueMasked (т***-style masking), dialogueClean (safe rewrite).
WHY: Punchlines are often profanity-based — three fallback layers
let the joke still get a speech bubble without failing moderation.

## Create New Table (if not found)
WHAT: Creates a new spreadsheet with two tabs (`Used Jokes`, `State`)
in one call, then creates a Drive folder for generated images.
KEY FIELDS: title = table name (⚠️ configurable — see setup checklist
on the main note), sheetsUi.sheetValues defines both tabs.
WHY: Table structure is defined once here so nothing needs manual
creation later — headers are seeded by the next two node groups.

## Seed "State" Row & Set Defaults
WHAT: Appends the first State row (current_page, row_id,
images_folder_id, document_id), then outputs the same 4 defaults
downstream so the very first "Build Page URL" call has everything
it needs without reading the sheet back.
KEY FIELDS: current_page=1, row_id=2 (fixed row to update later),
images_folder_id from Create Images Folder, document_id from
Create spreadsheet.
WHY: Avoids an extra round-trip read of the sheet we just wrote to.

## Build URL & Scrape
WHAT: Normalizes input from EITHER branch (snake_case from sheets,
camelCase from loop iterations) into one consistent camelCase shape,
builds the anekdot.ru tag-page URL for the given page number, then
fetches the raw HTML.
KEY FIELDS: page, rowId, imagesFolderId, documentId, attempt — all
camelCase from here on, used by every downstream node via
$('Build Page URL').
WHY: Single normalization point means downstream nodes never care
which branch or loop iteration produced the data.

## Extract & Filter Jokes
WHAT: Parses <div class="text"> blocks from the HTML, strips tags/
entities, keeps only jokes between 60–120 words, hashes each for
dedup, then checks if any candidates were found on this page.
KEY FIELDS: candidates[] (jokeText, wordCount, hash).
WHY: Word-count filter keeps jokes short enough for a single comic
panel; hashing enables cheap dedup lookups later.

## Pick First Unused Joke
WHAT: Reads all previously-sent hashes from "Used Jokes", then picks
the first candidate whose hash isn't in that list.
KEY FIELDS: alwaysOutputData=true (so an empty sheet doesn't break
the run), MAX_ATTEMPTS=15 pagination safety limit.
WHY: alwaysOutputData avoids a hard failure on a fresh/empty history
sheet; MAX_ATTEMPTS prevents an infinite loop if the tag runs dry.

## Assemble Comic Prompt
WHAT: Parses the AI Agent's JSON, picks bubble text per character via
a 3-tier fallback (dialogueRu → dialogueMasked → dialogueClean), and
assembles the final image-generation prompt with position + bubble
tail direction per character.
KEY FIELDS: BAD_PATTERN regex (code-level safety net on top of the
model's own dialogueSafe self-check).
WHY: Never trust the model's self-moderation alone — the regex catches
slang the model might not flag.

## Generate Comic Image
WHAT: Calls OpenRouter's image endpoint (Nano Banana 2 Lite,
resolution 1K), extracts the base64 payload, converts it to a binary
PNG file.
KEY FIELDS: model = google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image, aspect_ratio
1:1.
WHY: This model was chosen after comparing 5 options — best balance
of Cyrillic text legibility vs. cost (~$0.034/image).

## Store Image on Drive
WHAT: Uploads the PNG to the images folder, then shares it with
"anyone with the link, reader" so the URL works in Telegram/Sheets.
KEY FIELDS: name = hash.png, folderId from Build Page URL.
WHY: Uses .first() (not .item) for hash — pairedItem links break
across independent API-call nodes upstream.

## Send to Telegram
WHAT: Builds an HTML caption with the full joke text (truncated to
Telegram's 1024-char limit), then sends the photo + caption.
KEY FIELDS: binary pulled from Convert to File (not the previous
node) — non-Code nodes replace binary data otherwise.
WHY: A silent binary-loss bug cost real debugging time earlier —
always source binary from its original Code node.

## Update Current Page (only if it moved)
WHAT: Compares the page the joke was found on against the page the
run started on; only calls Sheets to update `current_page` if they
differ.
KEY FIELDS: matches on row_id (stable), not current_page (the value
being changed) — matching on the field you're updating never finds
the row.
WHY: Most runs find a joke on the very first page — skipping the
write saves an unnecessary API call in the common case.

## Record Sent Joke
WHAT: Appends hash, first-60-chars excerpt, timestamp, and Drive
image URL to "Used Jokes" — the dedup source of truth.
KEY FIELDS: all 4 values read via .first(), not .item (same
pairedItem-break reason as above).
WHY: This is the row "Get Used Hashes" checks against — if this
write fails silently, duplicate jokes can get sent later.

## ⚠️ CONFIGURE: Table Name
Must match exactly in BOTH "Search files and
folders" (queryString) and "Create spreadsheet"
(title). Any name works — this is just how the
workflow finds/creates its own data table on
your Drive.

## ⚠️ CONFIGURE: Drive Folder Name
Name of the Drive folder where generated comic
images are stored. Optional to rename — default
is fine, just needs to be something you recognize.

## ⚠️ CONFIGURE: Telegram Chat ID
Currently a placeholder — replace "YOUR_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID"
with your own channel/chat numeric ID before running.
Sending with the placeholder will fail.

## ⚠️ CONFIGURE: Source Tag
const tag = 'вовочка' — the anekdot.ru tag/category
being scraped. Change to any other tag on the site
to pull a different joke category.

## ⚠️ CONFIGURE: Image Model
Default: google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image
Compared against 4 alternatives — best balance of
Cyrillic text legibility vs. cost (~$0.034/image).
Swap the model string here to use another OpenRouter
image model.

## ⚠️ CONFIGURE: Chat Model
This node ships with NO model preset — you must pick
one manually in the node UI before running. Recommended:
google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite (fast, cheap, reliable JSON).

## Retry on Moderation Block
WHAT: If OpenRouter/Gemini rejects the image (IMAGE_SAFETY or similar),
the error branch logs that joke's hash to "Used Jokes" with
image_url = "BLOCKED_BY_MODERATION", then loops back to
"Get Used Hashes" — not to page scraping — so the next unused
candidate from the SAME page is tried, with no extra HTTP request.
WHY: Some punchlines can't be safely rendered even with masking/
clean rewrites; skipping them (instead of failing the whole run)
keeps the bot posting. Safety net against infinite loops is
Try Pick Joke's own MAX_ATTEMPTS (15 pages) — no separate counter
needed here.
